{{Quote|We've analyzed their attack, sir, and there is a danger. Should I have your ship standing by?''"<br />"''Evacuate? In our moment of triumph? I think you overestimate their chances!|Moradmin Bast and Wilhuff Tarkin|audio=BastTarkin.flac|<ref name="anh" />}}
'''Moradmin Bast''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dura-Kahn]]. An [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial]] [[General/Legends|general]], Bast was stationed on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] planet-destroying [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], where he served as the [[Chief/Legends|chief]] personal [[Aide/Legends|aide]] to [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] and the subordinate to [[High General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]]. In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], Bast was present for a meeting in the [[Battle station/Legends|battle station's]] [[Death Star conference room/Legends|conference room]], discussing the lost [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]], which had been [[Battle of Toprawa|stolen]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] began, Bast received information that the Rebels had found a small vulnerable [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] in the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star's]] superstructure. Since the exhaust port was a danger to the battlestation, Bast wanted Tarkin to evacuate the Death Star, although the Grand Moff believed that the Imperial forces would thwart the Rebels' attack. However, after the Rebel [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] successfully launched a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] into the Death Star's thermal exhaust port, the Death Star exploded, [[Death/Legends|killing]] Bast and everyone else on board.

==Biography==
===Service aboard the Death Star===
[[File:BastTarkinEvacuate-ANH.png|thumb|left|260px|Bast confers with Tarkin on the Death Star.]]
Moradmin Bast, a [[Human/Legends|Human]], hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dura-Kahn]].<ref name="imps"/> At a young age, Bast learned patience and cunning abilities by [[Big game hunter/Legends|hunting big-game]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Chief Bast}}</ref> Bast also saw the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] as a threat while growing up and believed that it should not be underestimated.<ref name="imps" />

At some point, Bast enlisted in the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] and eventually attained the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[General/Legends|general]]. Prior to the start of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="ds" /> which began in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> the general was assigned to serve as the subordinate to [[High General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]], the head of [[Army Operations]] aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]].<ref name="ds" /> In this capacity, Bast frequently acted as the [[Chief/Legends|chief]] personal [[Aide/Legends|aide]] to [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]],<ref name="Bast CSWE" /> the battlestation's lead [[Commander/Legends|commander]].<ref name="Tarkin">{{CSWECite|III|220|Tarkin, Grand Moff Wilhuff}}</ref> [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], the head of [[Navy Operations]] aboard the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], feared Bast and Tagge, due to their loyalty and respect toward Tarkin.<ref name="ds" />

Shortly before the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]]<ref name="anh" /> in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> Bast attended a [[Death Star conference room/Legends|staff conference]] on the battlestation. The Death Star's [[Commander/Legends|command]] staff&mdash;which included Tarkin, Tagge, and Motti&mdash;discussed the Rebel Alliance and its possession of the Death Star's [[Death Star plans/Legends|technical schematics]],<ref name="anh" /> which had been stolen by the Rebels during the [[Battle of Toprawa]].<ref name="Rebel">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> Believing that the Death Star was "the ultimate power in the [[Universe/Legends|universe]]," Motti wanted to use the [[Space station/Legends|station]] to threaten the Rebels, although the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] reassured Motti that the Death Star's destructive capability was insignificant next to the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. Throughout the conference, Bast sat in silence and witnessed Motti's near [[Death/Legends|death]] as Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force choked]] him for his lack of faith in the Force.<ref name="anh" />

===Death at Yavin===
[[File:BastTarkinFireWhenReady-ANH.png|thumb|right|270px|Tarkin gives an engineer the order to fire the Death Star's superlaser on Yavin 4.]]
Following the [[Rescue of Princess Leia/Legends|rescue]] of [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] aboard the Death Star, Tarkin was able to locate the Rebels' secret headquarters after having a [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]] attached to the princess's getaway [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|freighter]]. Tracking the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]], the Death Star approached its target&mdash;[[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], home of the [[Great Temple/Legends|Rebel base]]. Before the Death Star could fire on Yavin 4, the station had to [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around the planet [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]]. The battlestation's presence triggered the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] as the Rebels attempted to exploit a weakness in the battlestation's superstructure by launching [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into a small [[Thermal exhaust port/Legends|thermal exhaust port]] that led directly to the Death Star's main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]].<ref name="anh" />

However, the Rebels were not the only ones to discover this flaw. As the battle raged, military analysts informed Bast that the vulnerability of the thermal exhaust port in the face of the Rebel [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] attack posed a real danger to everyone aboard the battlestation. Wary of the Rebels' cunning,<ref name="imps" /> Bast immediately brought this information to Tarkin in the Death Star's [[Overbridge (Death Star I)/Legends|overbridge]] and inquired whether the Grand Moff wished to have his ship ready for evacuation, but Tarkin contemptuously brushed his recommendations aside. Despite his reservations, Bast remained with his superior [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] and watched as the battlestation approached Yavin 4.<ref name="anh" />

Once the Death Star cleared the planet, Tarkin, without hesitation, ordered a nearby [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] to fire the [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] on Yavin 4 to end the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="anh" /> However, [[Tenn Graneet]], the [[master chief petty officer]] responsible for firing the superlaser, momentarily hesitated.<ref name="ds" /> Graneet's delay allowed [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilot]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to successfully fire a pair of [[MG7-A proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into the thermal exhaust port before the superlaser was fired.<ref name="anh" /> Bast, as well as everyone stationed on the Death Star, was [[Death/Legends|killed]] when the massive battlestation exploded near Yavin 4.<ref name="Bast CSWE" />

==Personality and traits==
Moradmin Bast had no personal aspirations beyond serving the Empire and was loyal to Tarkin and Tagge aboard the Death Star.<ref name="ds" /> Some [[Officer/Legends|officers]] believed that Vader was a subordinate to Tarkin; however, Bast respected the Dark [[Lord/Legends|Lord]], since he witnessed how Vader dealt with foolish officers.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> A confident man who rarely underestimated his enemies,<ref name="Bast CSWE" /> Bast often praised the work that Tarkin had done on the Death Star.<ref name="ds" /> During the meeting aboard the Death Star prior to the Battle of Yavin, Bast remained quiet throughout. As Tarkin's chief personal aide, Bast became concerned for Tarkin's well being during the ensuing battle and delivered the Grand Moff information regarding the Rebel attack on the battlestation, including an offer to evacuate. However, Tarkin dismissed Bast's report as an overestimation of the Rebels' chances at victory, which ultimately cost the Grand Moff his life, as the Death Star was soon obliterated.<ref name="anh" />

Bast had [[Color/Legends|brown]] hair, lightly-colored [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and light skin. The Imperial general also had long sideburns on both sides of his face.<ref name="anh" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal===
Moradmin Bast was portrayed by [[Leslie Schofield]] in [[George Lucas]]' [[1977]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], originally credited as "Commander #1." In the final version of ''A New Hope'', Schofield played the character in two scenes.<ref name="anh" /> However, cut footage and dialogue of the character that was omitted from the final version of ''A New Hope'' was later included in the [[1978]] television program ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''.<ref name="hs">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> The footage was also made accessible in the bonus features of the ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' Blu-ray set, which was released in [[2011]].<ref name="blu-ray">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref>

The unnamed officer later received the name "Bast" in the [[1991]] [[West End Games]] sourcebook ''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''.<ref name="weg ds">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref> In [[1995]], Bast was first identified as "Chief Bast" in the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] ''[[Premiere Limited]]'' expansion set.<ref name="ccg" /> The [[2006]] novel [[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']] provided the Bast character the rank of general,<ref name="ds" /> while the article ''[[The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military]]'' from [[Star Wars Insider 96|''Star Wars Insider'' 96]] first identified Bast by first name&mdash;Moradmin.<ref name="imps" />

===''The Star Wars Holiday Special''===
The inclusion of Bast's deleted scene from ''A New Hope'' in ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' originally suggested that the character survived the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="imps" /> However, Bast's presence with Tarkin during the final moments before the Death Star's destruction in ''A New Hope'' shows that this is not the same officer. [[Lucasfilm]] [[Canon|continuity]] manager [[Leland Chee]] officially declared Bast a casualty of the battle through the [[StarWars.com Message Boards]].<ref name="chee1">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=480#13125742|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-10-24|time=12:08 PM|quote=Chief Bast - the Star Wars Encyclopedia said he died, so we consider him dead.}}</ref><ref name="chee2">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?messageID=15725996#15725996|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-02|time=11:01 AM|quote='''In fact, you once commented on this, saying that Bast's death couldn't be certain until another source is written on the subject.''' That was before someone pointed out to me that Bast is seen standing right next to Tarkin when he gives the order to fire when ready. Per the film, he's dead.}}</ref><ref name="chee3">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1185#16225670|thread=Holocron continuity database question|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2007-01-26|time=10:13 AM|quote='''This is what the Death Star Briefing pack says about Chief Bast: He is one of very few Imperial officers to successfully evacuate from the Death Star before its destruction. I thought that his survival wasn't supposed to be canon?''' The text was written and approved before we saw the evidence in the film to the contrary.}}</ref> The identity of the [[Unidentified Moradmin Bast look-alike|Bast lookalike]] from the ''Holiday Special'' was never officially explained.

===Inconsistencies===
[[Hasbro]]'s 2006 "Death Star Briefing" action figure multipack from the ''[[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]]'' line included a Chief Bast figure. The packaging noted that Bast was one of a handful of Imperial officers to evacuate the Death Star before its destruction.<ref name="hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=Death Star Briefing|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tscdeathstarbriefing.asp}}</ref> However, Leland Chee noted that the text was written before Lucasfilm had seen film evidence confirming Bast's death.<ref name="chee3" />

In both the ''A New Hope'' [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] and [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope (junior novelization)|junior novelization]], the officer who delivers Tarkin news of the Rebels' attack strategy during the Battle of Yavin is described as running from the room<ref name="anhN">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="anhJN">[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' junior novelization]]</ref> rather than remaining by Tarkin's side, as shown in the film.<ref name="anh" /> Despite elsewhere being mentioned by name and rank in the novel ''Death Star'', Bast's name is not mentioned during the Battle of Yavin. Instead, an operations [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] is described informing Tarkin of the thermal exhaust port danger.<ref name="ds">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>

Cassio Tagge's biography from the [[1998]] [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC]] program ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' mistakenly states that Tagge was the one who suggested Tarkin evacuate the Death Star during the Battle of Yavin, instead of Bast. However, in another section of the multimedia guide, Bast's character is correctly identified, including details of his biography from the character's ''SWCCG'' card.<ref name="bbm">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>

An Imperial officer corresponding to Bast's role appears in the 1977 [[Star Wars (1977)|Marvel]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]. The comic alternatively depicts Tarkin as giving the officer the order to analyze the Rebel attack and report back to him. After doing so, the officer then speaks Bast's line from the film, although the dialogue is significantly altered.<ref name="SW6">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref>

In the [[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]], Tarkin's exchange with Bast is placed in a very different context. Just before their conversation, Tarkin suggests to Admiral Motti that it may be prudent to leave the Death Star during the battle. Motti talks him out of it, saying that abandoning the station, even temporarily, would compromise his power and stop any hope the two have of sidelining Vader, or even the Emperor. Then when Bast suggests that Tarkin prepare a shuttle, the Grand Moff scoffs at the suggestion, pretending that he had not just been considering that very option.<ref name="Force and Counterforce">{{SWRadio|Force and Counterforce}}</ref>

The 2006 [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'' shows an Imperial officer contacting Tarkin via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] during the battle and speaking Bast's line from the film.<ref name="EaW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>
